title: Cannon Ball Tree: Ancient Cannonball Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: Flowers and fruit erupt straight from the bark. One grew from seed carried from Ceylon in 1931. Three cannonball trees mapped, Honolulu to Singapore.
intro: Couroupita guianensis grows its fruit and flowers straight out of the trunk rather than the branches, a habit botanists call cauliflory and gardens call a hazard: ripe cannonball-sized fruit falls from height and splits open with a smell that carries, and Honolulu's Foster Garden has posted a sign warning visitors under its specimen. Three trees on this site share the trick. Singapore's, in the Ginger Garden, grew from seed E.J.H. Corner carried aboard ship in 1931 during an eight-hour stop in Ceylon. Its flowers make no nectar; the sterile pollen at their centre exists only to bring carpenter bees in for the fertile kind elsewhere on the bloom. Oahu's second specimen, on the UH Manoa campus, carries a trunk 314 centimetres round and an unconfirmed campus legend that the playwright Thornton Wilder planted it in 1933. All three flower and fruit from bark most trees keep bare.
